P3 PLANNING ROUND (feat/p3-s1-outcome-label-seam, commit a3dbb03c) -- reconnaissance and slice plan, no code yet. The ticket was a blank placeholder (status planning, subtasks [], no prd.md, both jsonl files holding only the example line), so this round produced prd.md with thirty-odd file:line findings, a rewritten framing, four slices, the red lines, the refusals and four open rulings. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: the parent ticket lists four things and THREE OF THEM ALREADY EXIST -- offline quality vs online reward is already distinguished in storage (evaluator_samples.label_source is declared as "evaluator" | "engagement" | "human_review", evaluator_config.py:347, with engagement as its own JSONB column), the online reward is already collected for real (creator_note_stats in db/creator_stats.py:70-91 carries views/likes/comments/collects/shares and its own engagement_rate, fed by a 6225-line services/creator_stats/ subsystem with a 1576-line CDP client), LearningSignal -> ModelRevision already has a full lifecycle, and the two personalization stacks ALREADY SHARE A READ SEAM (memory/creator_agent_observations.py:111 implements the CreatorContentObservationSource protocol declared in creator_agent/observations.py:16, consumed by creator_agent/advisor.py:177). Nothing needs to be built. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS TWO CONNECTIONS, and both are proven, not inferred: (1) THE WEAK-LABEL FEED PATH DOES NOT EXIST. The only regular writer of evaluator_samples.engagement is agents/analyst.py:271-280, and its dict comprehension filters five keys (views/likes/collects/comments/shares) that publisher.py NEVER writes -- grep for those literals in publisher.py returns ZERO hits, and all twelve places that assign into publish_result carry error/error_type/recovery/result_known/note/publish_id metadata only. The gate is therefore always false. CORRECTED ON S1 DAY 1 (see prd.md section 9): the auto edge was removed, but analyst is NOT unreachable -- builder.py:187 continues 'It can be reached by resuming the workflow with phase=analyzing', state/modes.py:170/188 both map ANALYZING -> analyst, and api/routes/_wf_application.py:1818 is a complete manual trigger endpoint (assert_thread_owned + a has_analytics idempotence gate + Command(goto=["analyst"])). So the break is NOT 'nobody runs it', it is 'running it still cannot work': publish_result carries none of the five keys, and the manual path reads the same publish-time dict. Corroboration: label_source="engagement" appears ZERO times in backend/. (2) THE REAL METRICS NEVER REACH THE LEARNER. analytics.py contains ZERO references to evaluator_config / backfill_engagement / evaluator_samples / insert_sample, and the linker's product (link_status="linked", written only at analytics.py:894 and :908) is a REQUEST-TIME PROJECTION that is never persisted. evaluator_samples has no platform_post_id column while backfill_engagement(thread_id, ...) keys on thread_id -- so even a willing caller has no key to join on. CONSEQUENCE (assertable): count_labeled_since counts engagement IS NOT NULL, so it is identically 0, which is below MIN_EVOLVE_SAMPLES = 10 (evaluator_config.py:896), so maybe_evolve never leaves the below-threshold branch (evaluator_config.py:976-977) and train_weights / PromptEpoch never advance. THE WHOLE LOOP IS STRUCTURALLY COMPLETE, FULLY TESTED AND GREEN, AND HAS NEVER RUN ONCE -- the purest member of the 'declaration is not execution' family: evaluator_config.py's module docstring promises 'eventually trained from real engagement feedback', analyst.py:263 promises a 'weak label for grader finetuning', publisher.py:351 promises an explicit id match -- three declarations, zero data points. REFRAMING (same shape as P2c's 'not a missing Planner, a missing plan object'): P3 is not missing an Outcome Learning loop, it is missing the two wires that were designed into it. Consequence for slicing: no new module, no new Agent, no cross-module refactor -- each slice only has to make one existing wire actually carry current. SLICES: S1 make the situation visible and stop the bleeding (turn 'the loop never started' into a gate that goes red, and deal with analyst.py's always-empty back-fill, today's biggest source of misinformation). S2 lift the linker out of request-time projection into a reusable form and give evaluator_samples a nullable platform_post_id. S3 close the wire: after creator-stats/sync, back-fill real metrics into evaluator_samples.engagement with label_source="engagement", the first moment maybe_evolve is reachable. S4 the contract and gate condition document (docs/outcome-learning.md). S1's gate must distinguish 'never started' from 'ran and produced zero' -- those two are identical on all real data today (the same family as P2c-S5's 'a claim whose value is zero has no built-in control'), so it has to point at somewhere the thing DOES exist. OPEN RULINGS (all four carry the measured fact that decides them): (1) the parent's 'unify the two personalization stacks into a Memory Fabric' -- the READ side is already unified and no call site today reads both sides, so the write side is NOT consolidated; (2) merging decision-side LearningSignal (feedback-driven, pending_creator_review = human-gated) with engagement weak labels (automatic) would change the human gate's semantics, so NOT merged until a conflicting-conclusion instance exists; (3) whether creator_note_stats should re-drive sample recomputation -- deferred until S3 shows the re-back-fill cost (the table is an upsert and notes keep accruing); (4) MOST IMPORTANT -- what happens to the analyst node now that it is unreachable, since all three of its jobs (content_history metrics, weak-label back-fill, insights) silently stop happening when it does not run, while S1 must answer whether to restore its trigger or hand its duties to capability that already exists elsewhere. WHAT LANDED: the weak-label ingest contract is declared once. backend/db/evaluator_config.py
exports WEAK_LABEL_METRIC_KEYS (Final[tuple[str, ...]]) plus build_weak_label(payload), which
selects exactly the keys a payload carries; backend/agents/analyst.py calls it instead of
repeating the five keys. Behaviour is unchanged to the character -- `if k in payload` makes the
old `get(k, 0)` default unreachable -- and the misleading comment at the call site now states
the measurement instead of reading like working code.

THE GUARD: tests/unit/db/test_weak_label_contract.py (8 cases, 376 lines). The load-bearing one
registers the gap: the keys publish_result can carry (union of four AST shapes -- name-bound
dict, dict under the "publish_result" key, dict literal passed to _with_publish_link_metadata,
subscript writes; 15 keys today) do not intersect the contract, and the shortfall is asserted
to be all five. When the sync path starts writing metrics that test goes red on purpose.

EVERY SCANNER HAS A CONTROL, because a claim whose value is zero (checks 1 and 4) cannot have
one built in: gutting a scanner to `return set()` keeps it green. The controls are what make the
gap a measurement: the producer scan must still see post_id/post_url/status/publish_id plus the
three identity keys of the real _with_publish_link_metadata; a synthetic producer that does
write views/likes/comments/shares must be visible; the formula scanner must see a different key
set (impressions/saves); and label_source has exactly one writer, "evaluator", read as an AST
keyword argument so the comment in evaluator_config naming label_source="engagement" cannot
satisfy the scan.

WHAT S1 DID NOT DO (prd.md section 10): the "build a sample row with engagement and assert
maybe_evolve returns evolved" door from section 4 is NOT in S1, because such a row cannot be
built today -- backfill_engagement is only reached through the always-false `if engagement:`,
and building it needs real metrics, which is S3. Registered as S3's entry condition.
